This is the Sun! The Sun is a star. It's the closest star to us.
The Sun is so big that about one million Earths could fit inside it!
The Sun gives us light and keeps us warm. Never look right at it!
This is Mercury, the closest planet to the Sun. It's the smallest planet, too.

Mercury is covered in craters, just like our Moon.
On Mercury, you could jump more than two times higher than on Earth!
This is Venus, the hottest planet! It's even hotter than Mercury.
Thick clouds wrap around Venus like a big, hot blanket.
Venus spins backwards, so the Sun comes up on the other side of the sky!
On Venus, you would jump about the same as on Earth.
This is Earth, our home! It's the only planet we know with plants, animals, and people.
Most of Earth is covered by blue oceans. See the pink pin? That's where Amelia lives!
Earth spins around once every day. That's what makes day and night!
This is how high you can jump at home on Earth. Boing!
This is Mars, the red planet! It's red because its dirt is rusty.
Mars has the tallest volcano in the whole solar system. It's called Olympus Mons.
Robot rovers drive around on Mars and take pictures for us.
On Mars, you could jump more than two times higher than on Earth!
This is Jupiter, the biggest planet! More than one thousand Earths could fit inside.
See the big red spot? It's a giant storm, and it's bigger than the whole Earth!
Jupiter is a giant ball of gas. There's no ground to stand on!
Jupiter has no ground to stand on. But if you could stand on its clouds, you could only do a tiny hop. Jupiter pulls you down really hard!
This is Saturn, the planet with the beautiful rings!
Saturn's rings are made of billions of chunks of ice and rock.
Saturn is so light that if there were a bathtub big enough, it would float!
Saturn has no ground to stand on. But if you could stand on its clouds, you would jump about the same as on Earth.
This is Uranus. It rolls around the Sun on its side, like a ball rolling!
Uranus is an ice giant, and it's very, very cold.
Uranus has thin rings too, just like Saturn.
Uranus has no ground to stand on. But if you could stand on its clouds, you would jump about the same as on Earth.
This is Neptune, the farthest planet from the Sun.
Neptune has the fastest winds in the solar system. Whoosh!
Neptune is so far away that one trip around the Sun takes 165 of our years!
Neptune has no ground to stand on. But if you could stand on its clouds, you would jump about the same as on Earth.
This is Europa, one of Jupiter's moons. It's covered in ice!
Scientists think a giant salty ocean is hiding under Europa's ice.
Europa is a little smaller than our Moon.
On Europa, you could jump more than seven times higher than on Earth!
This is Titan, Saturn's biggest moon. It has a thick, orange, hazy sky.
Titan has lakes and rivers, but they are filled with liquid methane, not water.
Titan is even bigger than the planet Mercury!
On Titan, you could jump about seven times higher than on Earth!
This is the Moon! It goes around and around the Earth.
Astronauts have walked on the Moon. Their footprints are still there, because there's no wind to blow them away!
The Moon doesn't make its own light. It shines because the Sun lights it up.
On the Moon, you could jump about six times higher than on Earth!
This is Amelia's house, on planet Earth. Earth is the third planet from the Sun.
The Sun in our sky is the same star we visited in space. It looks small because it's very, very far away.
Earth is always spinning. When our side turns toward the Sun, it's day. When it turns away, it's night.

New Moon. The Moon's lit side faces away from us, so it looks dark.
Waxing crescent. A thin sliver of light is growing.
First quarter. Half of the Moon looks lit up.
Waxing gibbous. Almost full, and still growing!
Full Moon! The whole side facing us is lit by the Sun.
Waning gibbous. Now the light is shrinking.
Last quarter. The other half is lit now.
Waning crescent. Just a thin sliver is left before the new Moon.
Europa is one of Jupiter's moons, and it's a little smaller than our Moon.
Scientists think the ocean under Europa's ice may hold about twice as much water as all of Earth's oceans!
The reddish-brown stripes are long cracks in Europa's ice.
It's super cold here, much colder than the coldest place on Earth.
A spacecraft called Europa Clipper is on its way here to study Europa.
Titan is Saturn's biggest moon. It's even bigger than the planet Mercury!
Titan has a thick, hazy sky. That's why everything looks orange here.
Titan has lakes, but they aren't water. They're filled with a very cold liquid called methane.
On Titan it rains, but the raindrops are methane, not water.
In 2005, a probe named Huygens landed on Titan. A flying drone called Dragonfly will come here next!
Sunlight zooms to Earth in about eight minutes. That's super fast!
Getting to Mercury is tricky! The spacecraft MESSENGER took almost seven years to get there.
Some spacecraft flew to Venus in about four months.
Astronauts flew to the Moon in about three days.
The Perseverance rover took about seven months to fly to Mars.
The spacecraft Juno took about five years to reach Jupiter.
The spacecraft Cassini took almost seven years to reach Saturn.
The spacecraft Voyager 2 took about eight and a half years to reach Uranus.
Voyager 2 kept going, and it took twelve years to reach Neptune!
The spacecraft Europa Clipper left Earth in 2024. It will take about five and a half years to get to Jupiter and Europa.
The Huygens probe rode with Cassini for about seven years, then landed on Titan.
